articles.author: David Bianculli
articles.description: John Steinbeck's 1952 epic was first adapted to film in 1955 by director Elia Kazan. Now, Kazan's granddaughter Zoe has directed a new Netflix miniseries, starring Florence Pugh.
articles.title: Is our fate pre-destined? A new 'East of Eden' adaptation asks again

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: ennis Hastert, whose political legacy as Congress' longest-serving Republican House speaker was later fouled by allegations that he had molested high school athletes during his prior career as a teacher and wrestling coach, has died, a coroner said Monday. He was 84.
articles.title: Dennis Hastert, longtime Republican House speaker who went to prison, dies at age 84

articles.author: Heller McAlpin
articles.description: Like his previous work, including Homeland Elegies, The Radiance exposes the fissures of American racial, political and economic identity.
articles.title: Ayad Akhtar's 'The Radiance' addresses provocative subjects head-on

articles.author: Greg Myre
articles.description: The front line in the Russia-Ukraine war stretches more than 700 miles and has barely moved in four years. Yet straddling this line is the kill zone, dominated by constantly evolving drone technology.
articles.title: Drones buzz overhead, troops hunker underground in Ukraine's hellish kill zone

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The FBI and U.S. prosecutors say Wanying Zhang, also know as Heather, surveilled the Taiwanese president's son and his family.
articles.title: FBI arrests a woman accused of spying on Taiwan leader's family for China

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Talks between Khan's party and the government failed two days ago. Besides Khan's release, protesters demand his transfer to a hospital and family visits.
articles.title: Imran Khan supporters march in Pakistan to demand his release after talks failed

articles.description: The ongoing investigation has found the attacker intended to crash the plane into Israel's Ben Gurion International Airport, a person familiar with the matter but not authorized to speak publicly told NPR.
articles.title: FlyDubai attacker intended to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport, investigation finds

articles.description: The Nobel Prize in medicine was awarded Monday to three scientists working on the mechanisms the brain uses to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells.
articles.title: Nobel medicine prize goes to 3 scientists for research into brain activity

articles.description: A judicial spokesperson confirmed that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had filed a claim with the High Court in London and a hearing would take place Thursday.
articles.title: Former Prince Andrew files legal action to quash warrants that led to residence searches

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced early elections Monday after his government suffered a bruising legislative defeat last week on emergency measures related to the country's housing crisis.
articles.title: Spain's prime minister calls early elections as pressure mounts over housing crisis

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Key indicator dropped about 20% after the Reserve Bank last month announced the highest interest rates since 2011

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian households are the most persistently pessimistic they have been since the early-1990s recession, after a fourth rate rise this year.
Confidence among Australian consumers has plunged about 20% since the Reserve Bank of Australia lifted interest rates to the highest levels since 2011, according to the Westpac–Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment index.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australian consumer confidence plunges to worst level since 1990s after RBA rate rise

articles.author: Libby Brooks
articles.description:
In today’s newsletter: The party has voted to define Zionism as racist and back a single Palestinian state. But what does the policy mean, why has it caused alarm among Jewish members, and how will it impact the future of the Greens?
Good morning.
The Green party of England and Wales is in turmoil. Following a vote to adopt a policy that equates Zionism with racism, and calls for Israel to be replaced by a single Palestinian state “with equal rights for all”, some Jewish members say they are considering whether they are welcome in the party.
RAF Fairford | No 10 has insisted the Gloucestershire base is secure a day after the US air force suddenly withdrew a dozen B-1 bombers that had been stationed there amid security concerns about a possible threat from Iran.
Donald Trump | Donald Trump’s approval ratings reached a record low on Monday, according to new opinion polls. A new Reuters/Ipsos poll shows Trump’s approval rating at a record-low 32%.
Brazilian elections | Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, is poised to win the Brazilian presidency, after a shock first-round victory.
Jeffrey Archer | Jeffrey Archer, the bestselling author and former MP whose political career ended in disgrace when he was imprisoned for perjury, has died at the age of 86.
Cancer | Cases of seven types of cancer have risen sharply among younger people in England, major new research has found, prompting warnings that lifestyle choices are costing thousands of lives each year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tuesday briefing: Why the Green party’s Zionism vote has caused a backlash

articles.author: Adam Morton in Funafuti, Tuvalu
articles.description:
International leaders visit Tuvalu as part of climate talks co-hosted by Australia ahead of Cop31 conference
Pacific island leaders have urged a promised global transition away from fossil fuels must not be left open to renegotiation as they gather in tiny Tuvalu in a bid to build momentum before a major climate summit.
About 50 dignitaries – 14 national heads including Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, a list of climate change ministers and the heads of global agencies – flew to the low-lying atoll nation in a bid to bring attention to the plight of the countries most at risk from the climate crisis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Agreement to transition away from fossil fuels ‘not open for renegotiation’, Pacific leader tells pre-Cop

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
British banker Simon Andriesz helped to expose alleged ties between late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick
A top UK regulator has launched an investigation into how it handled a whistleblower – who highlighted alleged ties between the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick – after he took his own life.
The British banker Simon Andriesz died late last month aged 57, the campaign group Transparency Task Force, of which he was a member, confirmed over the weekend.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK regulator FCA to investigate how it handled Epstein whistleblower who took his own life

articles.author: Lucy Kassa
articles.description:
Civilians try to flee as men and boys rounded up on streets by new alliance as Ethiopia conflict erupts again
As renewed fighting has threatened a fresh humanitarian crisis in the northern region of Ethiopia, reports are emerging that a new alliance of armed groups in Tigray has been forcibly recruiting men and boys to its ranks.
Renewed conflict erupted on 23 September between Ethiopia’s federal government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which rules the region, shattering the fragile Pretoria peace agreement signed between the two sides in November 2022.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tigray rebel groups ‘forcibly recruiting boys as young as 15’ as fighting spreads

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
Mark Steele says he is ‘ashamed to be associated’ with the RSPCA Certified scheme, which badges 97% of chicken sold in Australia

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The vice-president of RSPCA New South Wales has left the animal welfare group, saying he is “sincerely ashamed” of the standards for RSPCA-certified chicken.
Mark Steele, a senior counsel who was a volunteer member of the board from 2021 and also served as a non-executive director of RSPCA Australia until March, issued a statement on LinkedIn outlining his decision to leave the group’s NSW branch for good at the end of September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RSPCA NSW director quits over welfare standards for RSPCA-branded chicken

articles.author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Researchers, who looked at UK, US and Dutch data, say lifestyle choices are costing thousands of lives a year
Cases of seven types of cancer have risen sharply among younger people in England, major new research has found, prompting warnings that lifestyle choices are costing thousands of lives each year.
The number of people under 50 diagnosed with prostate cancer in England has quadrupled since 2001, while early onset bowel, kidney and uterine cancer diagnoses more than doubled.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cancer rates rising more quickly among younger people, international study finds

articles.author: Amanda Meade
articles.description:
Radio host took teenager to lunch, had him visit his apartment, and told him to keep some conversations secret, court hears

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Alan Jones corresponded extensively with a 13-year-old who had written to him asking for financial help, showering the teenager with praise and asking him to keep some secrets from his mother.
The teenager, known as complainant A, posted a letter to Jones after his father left, a family member died and his single mother was struggling financially, the court heard on the first day of evidence given by complainant A in a closed court.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alan Jones corresponded with 13-year-old who asked for financial help, court hears

articles.author: Tom McIlroy and Sarah Basford Canales
articles.description:
Opposition leader says Coalition would reduce net overseas migration to 100,000 for two years 

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Angus Taylor says a Coalition government would reduce net overseas migration to 100,000 for two years, calling the plan “the biggest cut to immigration in the history” of Australia.
Following moves by One Nation and Labor to capitalise on growing anti-migration sentiment, the opposition leader announced plans by the Liberals and Nationals on Tuesday, promising net overseas migration rates of 130,000 in the third year and 160,000 in the fourth.
Tougher screening of visa applicants
Revising the temporary skilled priority list
Establishing a strike force to clear the backlog of skilled construction applications to address workforce shortages
Doubling the talent and innovation allocation to 7,000 places, through a new Aukus and Five Eyes visa
Linking each student visa to the enrolling institution
Introducing a new agriculture visa from 2030.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Angus Taylor vows biggest cut to migration in Australia’s history, slashing 650,000 temporary visas

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell, Shrai Popat, Keely Aouga and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the Breaking News US email


Ask our reporters your questions about the Iran war and the US midterms

As the supreme court hears oral arguments this morning, it’s worth noting that if the justices side with Boulder or decide that the case is not in their jurisdiction, then it would continue in state court.
But if the fossil fuel industry convinces the justices, the decision could apply not only to the Boulder case, but also to the many other climate cases brought by state and local governments around the US that we mentioned earlier.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump claims he’s ‘doing great’ as his approval rating sinks to record low – as it happened

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell and agencies
articles.description:
President’s U-turn comes after Democrats and Republicans condemned use of tax dollars for pro-Trump ads
Donald Trump said on Monday he would pay for taxpayer-funded, pro-Trump ads “with money I raised for MAGA, Inc.”, a political action committee, after the television advertisements glorifying himself sparked a major backlash.
In a social media post, Trump characterized the ads, which cost at least $1.5m in federal funds, as “a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A.” and called them “a rather standard thing to do”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says Super Pac will pay for taxpayer-funded ads that sparked outcry

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell and agencies
articles.description:
Nidal Hasan sentenced to death by military jury in 2013 for carrying out deadly shooting attack at army base in Texas
Donald Trump has approved the execution by US army firing squad of Nidal Hasan, who was sentenced to death for killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a social media post.
Hasan, who was an army psychiatrist, would become the first US soldier to be executed by the US military in more than 60 years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump approves firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter, Pentagon says

articles.author: Sam Levin, Keely Aouga and Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Hall housing Michael Kotlikoff’s office spray painted as demonstrators demand resignation of college president

Cornell University to take ‘serious look’ at fraternities after rape allegations

Mass protests erupted at Cornell University on Monday, with students criticizing officials’ handling of gang-rape allegations, demanding the president’s resignation and painting “SMASH THE PATRIARCHY” on an administration building.
Thousands of students and faculty gathered for a demonstration, sparked by the high-profile case of a former student known as Jane Doe, who said in a recent lawsuit that she was plied with drugs and raped at a fraternity house in 2024. The case has prompted international outrage and intense scrutiny of college fraternities and sexual violence on US campuses.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Student protests erupt at Cornell over mishandling of gang-rape allegations

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Exclusive: Guardian analysis finds more than 150,000 tonnes of fuel was shipped to Russian ports in July and August, some using sanctioned tankers 
Fuel is being shipped from South Korea to Russia via sanctioned tankers as Moscow scrambles for supplies amid the war in Ukraine, a move one expert said “undermines” Seoul’s public backing for Kyiv.
Guardian analysis of port records and ship-tracking data found that in July and August over 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mostly diesel, was loaded at several South Korean ports on to seven tankers that made 14 voyages to Russia’s far east.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fuel from South Korea being shipped to Russia as Ukraine war grinds on

articles.author: Esther Addley
articles.description:
English Heritage acquires film of first re-enactment, ‘a lot of pushing and shoving’ between Kent and Sussex students
At the top of a hill in a field near Hastings, a group of defiant English combatants awaited the invading army of William the Conqueror, brandishing their spears and shouting “Harold! Harold!”.
Unfortunately, the Norman army had been held up in traffic on the A27 from Brighton, meaning the most significant battle in English history had to be delayed by 20 minutes while the French got into their costumes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A God-almighty punch-up’: rare footage shows Battle of Hastings (the 1966 one)

articles.author: Lauren Gambino, Joseph Gedeon, Andrew Roth, Will Craft and Robert Tait
articles.description:
The war with Iran is reshaping America ahead of the midterms – how will it affect US voters at the polls? Join us for a live conversation on 6 October at 12pm ET with political and global correspondents

Sign in or sign up to join the conversation

Welcome to our latest US midterms live Q&A – just over a month away from election day on 3 November.
The war with Iran has had major implications for Americans’ wallets, government spending and US foreign policy. It’s has also been an important factor in reshaping the political landscape as the war enters its eighth month, with the 2026 US midterms quickly approaching.
The makeup of the Democratic party, plus key races to watch
Who are the groups financially backing the candidates in the midterms?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Iran war is unpopular, but will it cost Trump the midterms? Our reporters answer your questions

articles.author: Harry Cockburn
articles.description:
Publisher says author died peacefully at home ‘between writing sessions’
Jeffrey Archer, the bestselling author and former MP whose political career ended in disgrace when he was imprisoned for perjury, has died at the age of 86.
Archer, who was a Conservative MP for five years before serving as the party’s deputy chair, died “suddenly and peacefully” at his home “between writing sessions” on Monday, his publisher HarperCollins said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jeffrey Archer, former Conservative politician and novelist, dies aged 86

articles.author: Tom Phillips and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Progressive voters and supporters of incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva left reeling after far-right surge
Flávio Bolsonaro is in pole position to win Brazil’s presidential election, after a far-right tsunami propelled him to a shock first-round victory over the incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, leaving progressive voters reeling.
The 45-year-old rightwing candidate received 56.1m votes to Lula’s 53.8m – 47.03% to 45.16% – meaning the 80-year-old leftwinger has a mountain to climb if he is to bounce back in the second round on 25 October. Never, since the return of democracy to Brazil in 1985, has the first-round runner-up managed to turn the game around and win the second ballot.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro poised to win Brazilian presidency after shock first-round victory

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Government offensive launched under air cover by Saudi military coalition aims to retake all Houthi-held territory
Forces of the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen have recaptured several key areas around Bab al-Mandab strait from Iran-backed Houthi rebels, Yemeni officials said on Monday.
The officials said forces allied with the internationally recognized government have retaken the crucial town of Dhubab just north of the strait. They also captured the towns of Bab and Hadeid, said the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters. Witnesses said they saw government tanks and forces entering the towns.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi-backed forces recapture key areas around strait from Houthis in Yemen

articles.author: Aletha Adu, Peter Walker and Deborah Cole
articles.description:
European Green party says motion goes against its policy, with German Green co-leader calling it ‘intolerable and unacceptable’

Zack Polanski may rue lack of leadership when Greens needed him to act

The English and Welsh Greens are facing international ostracism after adopting a policy declaring Zionism as a form of racism, which has drawn dismay from the group representing European Greens.
The co-leader of the German Greens separately said the policy was “intolerable and unacceptable”, running contrary to its belief in the right of Israel to exist.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Green party of England and Wales facing international ostracism over ‘Zionism is racism’ vote

articles.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Experts say strength of evangelical church and stubbornness of Lula, 80, also helped propel Jair Bolsonaro’s son to first-round election win
On Sunday night, as the scale of the far-right triumph in Brazil sank in, an adapted football chant rang out in one of Rio’s most leftwing areas.
“Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa! Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa! Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa!” crestfallen progressives bellowed while drowning their sorrows after witnessing an excruciating election setback for their leader, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far right on the march and Lula’s failures: key drivers of Flávio Bolsonaro’s Brazil surge

articles.author: Jason Burke in London and Stephanie Kirchgaessner in Washington
articles.description:
Police and security agencies in multiple countries scramble to piece together background and intentions of Hamam al-Hammami
Investigators believe the co-pilot who tried to take control of a plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv last week originally planned his attack for July but postponed the hijacking, possibly because a friend was among the crew, regional and Israeli officials have said.
The evidence of prior planning suggests that Hamam al-Hammami, 29, may have specifically sought employment with an airline that flew to Israel in order to carry out the attack on last Wednesday’s flydubai ‌flight FZ1073, experts believe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flydubai co-pilot originally planned attack for July, investigators believe

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Tit-for-tat expulsions expected after relations deteriorate as a result of UK ban on goods from illegal settlements
The UK has threatened to expel one Israeli diplomat for every British diplomat forced to leave Israel as a result of Israel’s decision to close the UK consulate in East Jerusalem later this week.
This could mean as many as 27 Israeli diplomats being expelled from the UK, a step that would arguably mark the lowest point in British-Israeli diplomatic relations since the formation of the state of Israel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK threatens to expel Israeli diplomats over planned East Jerusalem consulate closure

articles.author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
articles.description:
Camera-enabled Meta spectacles are already restricted in UK and US because of fears about covert recording
Norway is planning a temporary ban on smart glasses in some public places, amid rising global concern at the spread of the AI-enabled recording devices.
The Oslo government is planning a bill to prevent the use of the camera-enabled spectacles in parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres, schools, daycare centres, healthcare facilities, gyms and public events, although private use would still be allowed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Norway plans temporary ban on smart glasses in some public places

articles.author: Jakub Krupa and Frances Mao
articles.description:
Hundreds of schools in France remain closed amid planned demonstrations across the country
The conservative People’s Party is very pleased with the announcement.
“At last,” they say on their X, with a slick election video – set to the EU’s anthem “Ode to Joy” – to go along with it.
Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez has called a snap election for 29 November, just days after rightwing parties blocked his minority government’s emergency measures on housing amid widespread protests (9:10).
The election will take place on Sunday, 29 November, the earliest possible date procedurally.
In a fierce address, Sánchez framed the election as choice between “regressing” under a “far-right coalition” or “keeping moving forward” with his progressive administration (9:04, 9:09, 9:17).
He said the election will be about who will guide Spain through a period of disruption amid high political tensions, global instability, climate emergency, and uncertainty posed by the rise of AI (9:13).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nearly 200 students injured in French schools protests as clashes with police continue – as it happened

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
Thousands expected to join marches of support on Tuesday across the country amid growing concerns over police response
France is bracing for a national day of protests and high-school blockades as a youth protest movement gathers pace amid a growing debate over the scale of the police response. 
In one incident, a 15-year-old protesting against what demonstrators said were France’s dilapidated ⁠and understaffed ​schools ‌had his hand ‌blown off outside a high school  in the northern town of Lens, said François-Xavier Lauch, the prefect of Pas-de-Calais.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: France braces for national day of school protests as boy loses hand

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Houghwith Dan Sabbagh; produced by Angus Neale; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
The US withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford after an investigation into an alleged planned terrorist attack on the base. At least 10 B-1 bombers used by the US military in the Iran conflict flew out of Fairford on Sunday, suggesting US officials were taking the threat seriously. Last week, five men in three vans near the military base were arrested, followed by a sixth British-Iranian national. All were released on bail, drawing criticism from the Pentagon. 
Lucy Hough speaks to Dan Sabbagh, the Guardian’s defence and security editor – watch on YouTube
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why did the US rush to withdraw bombers from RAF Fairford? - The Latest

articles.author: Pjotr Sauer and Luke Harding
articles.description:
Quarantine measures in place in several hospitals in eastern Russia amid uncertainty over death of Darya Shipilova
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, has said the US is closely monitoring the case of a Russian laboratory worker who died last week after a reported accident at a plague research institute in Siberia.
“We’re watching and monitoring it closely,” Rubio said on Monday before leaving for a trip to Europe. “I ⁠don’t think it’s cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and a cause just to keep an ⁠eye on it.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US closely monitoring case of lab worker who ‘possibly’ died of plague in Siberia, says Rubio

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Operation supported by 100 fighter jets said to have secured ‘air protection’ of Bab al-Mandab strait and destroyed hundreds of targets
Leaders of a Saudi-led coalition in Yemen claimed a broad air campaign involving 100 jet aircraft was under way on Monday against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea coastline and farther north in the capital, Sana’a.
The Saudi coalition spokesperson, Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki, said the 100 fighter jets participating in Operation Dawn of Yemen were providing support to forces of Yemen’s internationally recognised government.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Air campaign against Houthis under way in Yemen, says Saudi-led coalition

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Pakistani authorities insist marchers calling for former PM to be released from jail will not reach the capital
Imran Khan’s supporters have begun a march to Islamabad to demand his release from jail after efforts by the government to halt the protest failed.
The march began in the former prime minister’s stronghold province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in north-west Pakistan on Sunday, according to leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Supporters of Imran Khan start march on locked-down Islamabad

articles.author: Mohamed Gabobe in Mogadishu
articles.description:
After Guardian investigation uncovered drone strike that killed 12 civilians and injured many more, seven-year-old Abdiqadir Salah underwent vital operation in Mogadishu
On the rickshaw ride to the hospital, Marian Haji Abdi Guled felt a mixture of joy and apprehension: the day they had been waiting for had finally arrived.
Almost a year earlier, her then seven-year-old son, Abdiqadir Salah, had been seriously injured, alongside his two siblings, in what a Guardian investigation found was a US drone strike on the village of Jamaame in Somalia that killed at least 12 civilians, including eight children.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Guardian readers fund life-changing surgery for Somali boy injured in US airstrike

articles.author: Martin Patriquin in Montreal
articles.description:
Parti Québécois promises to hold independence referendum in Canada’s French-speaking region by 2028
Voters in Quebec are going to the polls in provincial elections which will probably result in victory for a party that has promised to hold a referendum on independence from Canada within the next two years.
If polls are correct, the Parti Québécois (PQ) will form the government of the province of roughly nine million, the first time that the separatist movement will have gained power in the French-speaking region for more than a decade.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Quebec poised to elect separatists to power for first time in more than a decade

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
Musician who had hit albums with Racine and Rats later became a judge on six seasons of Canadian Idol
Sass Jordan, the singer-songwriter who became a significant success in Canada’s rock scene in the 1990s before starring as a judge on Canadian Idol, has died aged 65.
No cause of death has been given. A statement on social media said she died on 2 October “surrounded by her loving family … She remains in our hearts, an inimitable force of nature. An irreplaceable being of light and joy!”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sass Jordan, Canadian rock singer-songwriter, dies aged 65

articles.author: James Michelin for MetDesk
articles.description:
Temperatures in US state forecast to hit high 30s celsius this week, while regions in Indonesia grapple with wildfires
The National Weather Service in the US has issued extreme heat warnings for parts of southern California, including Los Angeles, until Thursday, as temperatures are expected to hit the high 30s celsius. Burbank, a suburb north of Los Angeles, recorded 39C on Saturday, a few degrees shy of the October record for the region set in 1987. A persistent area of high pressure will remain in place this week, leading to further hazardous hot weather and increased fire risk.
Parts of Indonesia are in the midst of an extreme wildfire season, which has peaked over the past month. Western Kalimantan (Borneo) and southern Sumatra have been particularly badly affected. The lack of rainfall has dried the usually water-logged tropical soils, meaning that fires have been able to spread quickly, above and below the surface. Indonesia’s soils are also extremely rich in peat, meaning that the smoke produced from the fires contain higher levels of toxic gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide. Cities in surrounding areas and as far as Malaysia and Singapore have experienced reduced air quality in recent weeks as a result. Drought and wildfires are more common in this part of the world during El Niño events owing to suppressed thunderstorm activity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Extreme heat warnings issued for parts of southern California

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Study of remains taken from royal cemetery at Umm el-Qa’ab appears to confirm early Egyptologist’s theory
Court officials and craftspeople serving early Egyptian kings may have been sacrificed when their ruler died, according to research that found fractures in several ancient skulls.
The royal cemetery of Umm el-Qa’ab near Abydos features the tombs and enclosures of the First Dynasty rulers of Egypt, and dates as far back as 3,000BC.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Skull fractures suggest servants of Egypt’s ancient kings were sacrificed

articles.author: Seán Clarke and Tom Phillips
articles.description:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is standing against Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of the presidential race
Brazil’s president is directly elected: each voter’s ballot counts equally and there is no electoral college. If no candidate wins more than 50% of the valid votes cast in the first round, a second runoff election will be held three weeks later between the two candidates who polled highest.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil presidential election 2026: first-round live results

articles.author: William Christou in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Calls for release of six Matsadaash staff after one is charged, while whereabouts of other five remain unknown
An Egyptian journalist has been charged with joining a terrorist group, days after an entire newsroom was detained in what rights groups have said is a crackdown on press freedoms.
Last week, authorities arrested six journalists from the independent fact-checking and investigative platform Matsadaash – literally meaning “don’t believe” – accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and publishing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Egyptian journalist faces terrorism charges after entire newsroom detained

articles.author: Agence France-Presse and Guardian staff
articles.description:
Suspect allegedly killed woman at hotel in Okinawa as prime minister calls crime ‘exceptionally brutal and vicious’
A US marine stationed on Japan’s southern island of Okinawa is accused of murdering a Japanese woman and has been arrested on suspicion of murder, police said on Sunday.
The suspect allegedly “killed [a] 39-year-old woman at a hotel in Naha and stole her wallet” as well as her backpack, local police told news media outlets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US marine arrested in Japan on suspicion of killing woman, police say

articles.author: Alex Daniel
articles.description:
Britain under pressure to put tariffs on cheap Chinese vehicle imports ahead of protectionist trade measures
Britain’s car industry is grappling with a “difficult trade-off” between China and Europe, as manufacturers struggle to balance the benefits of both markets ahead of looming trade measures that could restrict UK exports to the EU.
The UK is an outlier in choosing not to put import taxes on Chinese vehicles, even as the US has shut them out almost entirely, and the EU imposes duties of up to 45%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK car industry faces ‘difficult trade-off’ between Chinese and EU markets

articles.author: Patrick Wintour
articles.description:
Western Libya’s GNU say working with Saddam Haftar ‘impossible’ as US-backed merger plan breaks down
Allegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.
Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA), has increasingly been seen by the US as an important figure in its plans to unify Libyan security, judicial and political institutions.

articles.description:
Three-quarters of nations have rightly abolished capital punishment in law or practice, but killing by the state has surged in the US
What is the kindest way to kill? That’s the question being asked once more following Tennessee’s failed attempts to execute Christa Pike for the brutal murder of a classmate, Colleen Slemmer, when she was 18. The 50-year-old was taken to a medical facility, her condition unknown, with witnesses describing her snoring loudly around 40 minutes after receiving two injections of pentobarbital on Wednesday. It is the second botched killing in months, prompting Tennessee’s governor to order a halt to executions.
Lethal injection was supposed to be the humane alternative to firing squads and electric chairs. They in turn were seen as an improvement on hanging, which looked much like lynching in a system disproportionately handing the death penalty to black men. The age and ill health of those executed, and the ethical refusal of most medical staff to be involved, may contribute to botched injections. But analysis of autopsy results has provided compelling evidence that suffering is inherent; injections – especially those involving paralytic drugs – have merely disguised it. What is described as safeguarding the dignity of prisoners is really about reducing the discomfort of witnesses who would otherwise see their suffering.

The actor will perform famous TV sketches – as well as new material created with Richard Curtis, Ben Elton and Howard Goodall – in Rowan Live, which opens in February

Bacon has long been a favourite of carnivores, but there is growing consumer concern about the health risks posed by nitrites, chemicals used to cure meats.

Citizen environmentalists create online platform that flags spills in real time and highlights repeatedly polluted spots 
The easy thing for the people who live on the banks of the River Dart in Devon might have been to grumble and groan about the sewage spills that blight their beloved waterway.

British farmers are experiencing the worst bluetongue season on record, with the number of cases surpassing the past three years combined.

The Traitors and big film shoots help boost economy but some highlight lack of opportunities for local talent
Scotland’s striking Ardross Castle, the oldest star of The Celebrity Traitors, which kicks off on Thursday night, is just one of the stops on the Scottish tourist board’s “screen tourism” trail. While global billionaires and multinational companies have been lured to its shores, many islanders feel left behind and priced out, with food bank use increasing

Growing up in Wales, Liz Puleston-Jones was familiar with the country’s rich heritage of storytelling and traditional music, but none of it ever seemed to have much of a connection to her life in Swansea.

articles.author: Keith Stuart
articles.description:
There’s no Leon, Claire or Ada Wong in Cregger’s adaptation. Instead, it re-creates something more fundamental – the strange, terrifying experience of actually playing the game
• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
I’ve been surprised by the number of Resident Evil fans complaining on social media about Zach Cregger’s cinematic adaptation of the survival horror series. “It’s not a real Resident Evil movie,” they’ve claimed. Were we watching the same film? Certainly, it doesn’t feature any of the familiar heroes – there’s no Leon, no Claire, no Ada Wong – and there’s a distinct lack of recognisable antagonists and well-known locations. Despite all of this, Cregger’s interpretation is one of the most accurate and interesting video game films ever made.
On the surface, it’s about a zombifying virus that gets accidentally released in Raccoon City by the Umbrella Corporation. These are, of course, the foundations of the Resi mythos. More interestingly, Cregger seeks to replicate and explore the structural and narrative conventions of the series. In the film, the player character, hapless courier Bryan Hodukavich, is thrust into a viral outbreak, with no weapons and no idea what’s going on. He is then submerged into an uncanny shadow world of escalating peril and body horror. The film takes us through a series of locations dragged straight from the games – an abandoned farmhouse, a road tunnel crammed with abandoned cars, a hospital and the obligatory sewer level. As he progresses, Bryan finds increasingly powerful weapons, from a handgun to an assault rifle – but he is always short on ammo. And there are typewriters in at least two scenes!

The gathered technologists were drawn to the idea of building a small nation-state dedicated to the endeavor, Reich recalls in “System Error: Where Big Tech Went Wrong and How We Can Reboot it”.
When Reich asked whether this state would be a democracy, he got a cool no. “Democracy is too slow, and it holds science back,” he was told. “To optimize for science, we need a beneficent technocrat in charge.”

The game generates blood-pumping moments as you twist, turn and weave through the skies, while your locked-on missiles speed away to obliterate an enemy plane
The core appeal of any Ace Combat game lies in the moment when the beautiful clouds part, the sunlight glints off your perfectly rendered state-of-the-art fighter jet, and guitar-shredding music kicks into overdrive as your locked-on missiles speed away to obliterate an enemy plane. All of that is 100% present in Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve. What’s new is the way it delivers its unexpectedly compelling story.
Set in the Earth-like alternative world of Strangereal, where every country is absolutely obsessed with fighter planes and giant superweapons, Ace Combat drafts you into the role of a fake ace pilot called the Wings of Theve – a propaganda invention to raise the morale of a besieged nation, similar to real-life rumours about Ukraine’s Ghosts of Kyiv. You rapidly find yourself becoming an actual legendary pilot, soaring through the skies with your buddies and raining hell upon your oppressors as everybody cheers on the radio. Speaking of ghosts, you have one in your ear – your predecessor, whom nobody else can hear, a gravelly voice waxing lyrical about flying, war and whatever else is on his mind as you flit about.

I have spent the last three weeks living with my 22-year-old son in a two-bedroom flat he has dubbed the ”brotel”. We cook curries and watch Lanterns. We barbecue meat and analyse Tarantino movies. We get pizza and we play video games. Boy, do we play video games!
The first game I ever played in co-op with him was Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 in 2009, when he was five. He wasn’t the most accomplished sidekick, not so great at placing a mobile gun turret while under fire from what seems like a bazillion enemy soldiers, but we had a laugh. It started the video game bond between us before his sister introduced him to Banjo-Kazooie and Rayman, and he stopped being a preschool warmonger. Probably for the best. So how would it be tackling the same game nearly two decades later?
